title: Invariant coverage tax: totality versus proportionality

completion_criteria.text: Map the enforcement chain end to end and write it down: registry, coverage entry, checker modes, CI wiring, and exactly where the seventeen-row obligation is generated
Measure the real cost rather than assert it: what a full coverage entry actually costs on a low-risk change, and how that scales as the registry grows past seventeen ids
Settle against M1 and M2 as ratified: does proportional coverage necessarily reintroduce the self-selected allowlist M2 forbids, or is there a form that does not
Choose one resolution on robustness first then simplicity, record the decision, and name explicitly what it gives up
Implement it with red-before/green-after receipts and its own coverage entry, then ship one PR via pr-create

spine.active_goal: Land 0273's inert basis as one atomic change, but only after 0278's checker-enforced kind rule replaces hand-authored globs.

open_risks.text: Ship nothing from feat/invariant-inert-registry until both the glob data and the checker are fixed — the data has two proven routes to a false INERT verdict and the checker has two verified criticals

A coverage entry whose filename carries a non-ASCII byte is permanently unscoped and its inert rows are never verified — a durable forgery slot, not a one-shot, so fix the path rendering before anything lands

Widening a glob is self-authorizing in one green pull request — any glob broad enough to be worth adding absorbs the registry file itself, so the same change proves its own new basis unless a breadth floor bars it
The checker and the registry data must land as ONE commit range — inert_when data whose committed checker never reads it is a dormant basis a later pull request can lean on
The evaluator exists only as an uncommitted working tree and a saved patch — a branch switch or a reset by a concurrent session loses it
A second session works this same repo and switched the shared checkout mid-session — check the branch and working tree before assuming either is where you left it

npm test carries one permanently red environmental failure that will mask a real regression — the global settings file is a real file, not a symlink into the repo, so the config-protection guard is inert

key_decisions.title: Invariant coverage cost measured: 76.3k fixed plus 2,298 tokens per row, linear and unbounded
Adopt the registry-declared inert predicate, paths-only, with M3/M4/M5 structurally barred from carrying it
Hand-authored inert globs are not survivable; the declarable class must be enforced by a checker kind rule

out_of_scope: Moving the verdict into the PR body - pr-create's flag set is closed and its values cap at 200 characters, which is why M1 puts the verdict in a committed artifact
Any resolution needing a second reviewer, a bot account, or org-level infrastructure - this is a solo owner-held repo
